From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter
Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of
Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and
look forward to your mark-up.
SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)
Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims
is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.
Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and
only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the
basket is recoverable.
Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after
Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims
unless expressly stated otherwise.
Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same
caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.
Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and
non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.
Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public
registers (see Disclosure Letter).
Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the
Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or
public records.
Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller
will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the
counterparty's written consent.
Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding)
will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.
Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing
bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds
flow.)
Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio
matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.
Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter
and is not expected to be material.
Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course
operating costs.
Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime
above.
Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.
Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and
records are fictional.
1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the
indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including
DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly
searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific
disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent,
payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.
2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause
11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final
written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.
3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2.
As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security
is included.
4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of
every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of
non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.
5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject
to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft
Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or
on-costs apply.
6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external
email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity
timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised
person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation
remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no
loss amount.
7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as
a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.
8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each
(AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether
each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.
9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale
consent is required merely because shares are sold.
10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of
the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the
Buyer has completed its own verification.
11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer
must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Positions

**Bottom line:** The Seller's package shifts most known risk to the Buyer. Four provisions work together to do this: the general disclosure of the whole data room (DL 1.1-1.2 and Schedule 7), the anti-sandbagging clause (8.3), the non-reliance and exclusive-remedy language applying to all claims, and the 20% cap. Because the Seller has already disclosed the Riverlark, Bluefen, Ironquay, bonus and privacy matters, those items would be carved out of any warranty claim, leaving the Buyer with no remedy for them unless specific indemnities are added. The package also treats several conditions and payments as post-Completion problems. I recommend rejecting the package as drafted and returning a Buyer mark-up built around specific indemnities, price-mechanics fixes and conditions precedent.

*This is a commercial and drafting review, not a substitute for NSW/Australian advice. The points on privacy, tax and limitation periods should be confirmed by specialist counsel before they go into a mark-up.*

---

## 1. Structural issues (highest priority)

**a) General data room disclosure (DL 1.1, 1.2; Schedule 7).**
The Seller discloses "every fact, matter and circumstance" in the data room and public registers. That would qualify every warranty by reference to thousands of documents, and the Buyer would have to find the disclosure in the data room to know what it had accepted. Australian practice generally requires fair, specific disclosure against identified warranties. The Buyer should reject general disclosure entirely. The only acceptable disclosure is specific, fairly disclosed against a numbered warranty, with copies of documents attached. Public searches should not count as disclosure.

**b) Buyer knowledge / anti-sandbagging (cl 8.3).**
The clause bars claims for any matter the Buyer "or its advisers had knowledge of," including anything "discoverable" from the data room. Combined with 1(a), it would prevent claims for every issue in DD-002 to DD-012. Buyers normally want the reverse: a pro-sandbagging clause making the Buyer's knowledge irrelevant to warranty claims. Known issues are then handled through specific indemnities, not through warranties the Buyer is assumed to have waived. Whether knowledge defeats a claim at general law is not settled enough to rely on, so the SPA must say it expressly.

**c) Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applied to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3, 12.8, 20.5).**
As drafted, these would apply to fraud, fundamental warranties and tax claims. Fraud must be carved out of non-reliance and the cap, and the exclusive-remedy clause should not cut off specific indemnities or equitable remedies. The Buyer should also insist that nothing in the Agreement limits liability for fraud or wilful concealment.

**d) "Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (cl 12.3/13).**
This is a drafting trap. Limitations should attach only to general warranty claims, with each category stated expressly. Flip the default so that caps, thresholds and time limits apply only where the clause says so.

**e) Fundamental and title warranties on the same caps and time limits.**
Capacity and title should sit outside the general regime: cap at the full Purchase Price, no de minimis or basket, and a longer time limit (commonly six years or more).

---

## 2. Financial exposure: the general warranty regime

| Term | Seller position | Buyer concern | Pushback |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cap (cl 12.1) | 20% of price = AUD 4.8m | Buyer carries 80% of general warranty risk | Increase to at least 30-50% or price. Consider W&I insurance as an alternative. |
| De minimis (cl 12.2) | AUD 25,000 per claim | Small related claims excluded | Reduce to AUD 10,000 or lower; ensure related claims aggregate; confirm de minimis claims count toward basket. |
| Basket (cl 12.2) | AUD 250,000, deductible ("excess only") | Buyer absorbs the first AUD 250k of every loss | Change to a tipping basket (once exceeded, recover from the first dollar). Clarify whether the cap includes or sits on top of the basket. |
| General time limit (cl 12.3) | 18 months | Too short for tax, compliance and IP exposures to surface | Push for 24-36 months. Tax, privacy and IP claims should run longer. |

The deductible basket matters more than it looks. On a AUD 24m deal, a AUD 250k deductible is around 1% of price, which is within the normal range, but a deductible rather than a tipping structure means the Buyer always bears the first AUD 250k of every loss.

---

## 3. Specific known issues

**Riverlark Bank facility (cl 2/7; DL 3).**
About AUD 3.2m is outstanding, the facility has not been repaid, and the security has not been discharged. The Seller proposes a release "following Completion."
- Under a debt-free/cash-free deal, the outstanding amount should be paid out from the Purchase Price at Completion, against a payoff letter and executed discharges (including PPSR discharge and release of any guarantees or security over Company assets).
- If the Seller's approach stands, the Buyer may have to fund the AUD 3.2m itself to get the Company free of secured debt, and it would carry the risk of the lender not releasing.
- **Pushback:** Make a payoff letter and discharges a condition of Completion, with the payoff amount deducted from price. Include accrued interest, fees and break costs in the payoff figure.

**Bluefen consent (cl 3/6.3; DL 2).**
Bluefen accounts for about AUD 3.6m, roughly 30% of FY26 revenue. Its change-control consent is conditional under clause 11.3 and has not been obtained. The Seller proposes "reasonable endeavours" and to treat consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. That wording lets the Seller decide whether the condition is met, and does not require the consent to be unconditional.
- **Pushback:** Make a final, unconditional Bluefen consent (or satisfaction of the conditions in cl 11.3, evidenced in writing) a condition precedent for the Buyer's benefit, waivable only by the Buyer. Require "all reasonable endeavours" with the Seller bearing any consent fees or concessions. If the consent is not obtained, the Buyer should have a termination right, or a price adjustment if it elects to complete. Add a specific indemnity for loss of Bluefen revenue or margin in the first 12-24 months if the Buyer completes without the consent.

**Ironquay IP (cl 11.1; DL 4).**
Transfer of SOW3 Project Materials is conditional on payment of every SOW3 fee under clause 7.3 of the Ironquay agreement. AUD 180,000 is recorded as open, and there is no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room. The Seller's indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and described as "adequate."
- The Buyer may not own the Project Materials at Completion, and the indemnity does not cover title, third-party claims or other SOWs.
- **Pushback:** The Seller pays the AUD 180k before Completion (or it is treated as Debt), and the Buyer receives a receipt and a confirmatory assignment of the Project Materials as a condition of Completion. Replace the SOW3-only indemnity with a specific IP indemnity covering title to Project Materials, infringement claims and any other Ironquay SOWs, outside the cap and basket.

**Employee bonuses (DL 5; funds flow).**
AUD 420,000 in conditional Completion bonuses is excluded from the funds flow and described as "a matter for the Seller." That is not acceptable. Bonuses triggered by the transaction are normally debt-like items, and the Buyer should not inherit them. The disclosure also does not address payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs.
- **Pushback:** Treat the bonuses, and all associated employer costs (payroll tax, superannuation, on-costs), as Debt or a transaction liability deducted from price. Quantify the full employer cost, confirm the vesting conditions, and require the Seller to pay all bonuses that vest on or before Completion. Add a warranty that no other transaction, retention or change-of-control payments are owed.

**Export/privacy incident (cl 4.6/Sch 6; DL 6).**
DD-006 records a download link sent to an unintended external address. The export may contain about 1,240 records with names, business emails, roles and activity timestamps. The investigation is preliminary, and the Seller says the matter is "not expected to be material."
- Records of this kind may include personal information under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth). If there is an eligible data breach, the Company must carry out an assessment (generally within 30 days of becoming aware of a suspected breach) and notify the OAIC and affected individuals where required. Because the data room is dated 22 September 2026 and it is now 6 November 2026, the Buyer should urgently confirm whether this assessment has been completed and whether any deadlines have already passed.
- **Pushback:**
  - Require the Seller to commission forensic investigation and complete the notifiable data breach assessment before Completion, at its cost, with the findings shared with the Buyer.
  - Add a specific, uncapped indemnity (or one capped at price) for losses from the incident, including investigation, notification, regulatory penalties, remediation and third-party claims, outside the basket and de minimis.
  - Add a privacy and data-security warranty, with a longer time limit.
  - Consider a retention or escrow sized to the potential exposure until the investigation concludes.
  - Reject the Seller's "not expected to be material" statement as a warranty or characterisation. It is not a disclosure.

**Supplier renewals (DL 8; cl Sandbar).**
Three renewals totalling AUD 330,000 are described as ordinary course. The disclosure does not say whether they are terminable, accrued or unavoidable. Read together with DD-008 and DD-011, they may overlap in timing or scope, and the aggregate figure should be checked for double counting.
- **Pushback:** Confirm each contract's terms, termination rights and whether any commitments extend beyond Completion. Treat unavoidable post-Completion commitments as Debt or a working capital adjustment as appropriate. Add an interim covenant that the Seller will not renew, extend or vary material contracts without Buyer consent.

**Office lease (DL 7).**
The disclosure refers to a notification obligation but does not say whether landlord consent is needed for the share sale.
- **Pushback:** Seek a landlord consent or estoppel as a condition precedent if the lease is triggered by a change of control.

**Mossvale (DL 9).**
The assignment restriction is not confirmed as triggered by the share sale.
- **Pushback:** Obtain a written legal view or counterparty confirmation. If consent is required, make it a condition precedent.

**Title (DL 10; DD-012).**
The share register shows Harbourglass as holder of 100% of issued shares, but the disclosure states that the Buyer has not verified title.
- **Pushback:** Run independent ASIC company and register searches and a PPSR search for encumbrances over the shares. Obtain original share certificates, executed transfer forms and confirmation of no options, convertible instruments or other rights over shares. Make title a fundamental warranty, with the Seller giving a title indemnity.

**Tax and IP (general regime).**
The Seller considers these "settled under the general regime." They are not settled.
- **Pushback:** Add a pre-Completion tax indemnity on a pound-for-pound basis, outside the cap, basket and de minimis, with a time limit that runs for the full ATO amendment period plus a buffer. Add standard tax warranties and conduct-of-audit provisions. Add IP ownership and non-infringement warranties, with specific IP indemnities as noted above.

---

## 4. Missing protections

The Seller's package is silent on:
- **Security for claims.** Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd may be a holding vehicle that distributes proceeds after Completion. Seek a retention or escrow, or a parent company guarantee.
- **Interim covenants** (conduct of business, no new contracts without consent, notification of breaches).
- **Termination rights** if conditions are not satisfied by a long-stop date.
- **Bring-down of disclosure** to the Completion date. The disclosure is stated as at 22 September 2026, more than six weeks ago.
- **Warranty insurance** as an option to supplement or replace part of the cap.

---

## 5. Summary of recommendations

**Priority 1 (deal-critical; resolve before any further negotiation):**
1. Reject general data room disclosure (DL 1.1, 1.2, Sch 7). Require specific disclosure against numbered warranties only.
2. Reject the buyer-knowledge bar (cl 8.3). Insert a pro-sandbagging clause.
3. Carve fraud out of the non-reliance, exclusive-remedy and cap provisions.
4. Require Riverlark to be repaid from price at Completion, with a payoff letter and discharges as a condition.
5. Make an unconditional Bluefen consent a condition precedent, with a specific indemnity or price adjustment if it is not obtained.
6. Require the AUD 180k Ironquay payment and a confirmatory IP assignment before Completion, and replace the SOW3-only indemnity with a broader IP indemnity.
7. Treat the AUD 420k bonuses and employer costs as Debt or transaction liabilities in the funds flow.
8. Urgently confirm the status of the privacy incident and NDB assessment. Require forensic investigation and a specific indemnity outside the cap and basket.

**Priority 2 (commercial and drafting):**
9. Raise the general cap (from 20% to at least 30-50% of price, or consider W&I insurance).
10. Reduce the de minimis (to AUD 10k or lower) and replace the deductible basket with a tipping basket.
11. Extend the general time limit to 24-36 months.
12. Fix the "all Claims" limitation default so limitations apply only where expressly stated.
13. Treat fundamental and title warranties separately: cap at price, no thresholds, six-year time limit.
14. Add a pre-Completion tax indemnity outside the cap and basket, with an ATO-based time limit.
15. Add IP ownership and non-infringement warranties.

**Priority 3 (verification and administrative):**
16. Confirm the Sandbar renewal terms and check for double counting across DD-008 and DD-011. Add an interim no-new-contracts covenant.
17. Obtain landlord consent or estoppel for the office lease if the share sale triggers it.
18. Confirm whether the Mossvale restriction is triggered and obtain consent if required.
19. Run independent title verification (ASIC, PPSR, original share certificates, transfer forms).
20. Add interim covenants, termination and long-stop rights, a bring-down of disclosure, and security for claims (retention, escrow or parent guarantee).

**Immediate next steps:** Confirm the status of the privacy assessment; obtain the Riverlark payoff figure and Bluefen consent position; reconcile the funds flow against the debt-free/cash-free price mechanics (including Riverlark, bonuses and the Ironquay payment); and send the Seller a mark-up that rejects Priority 1 items outright.
